title: Put a shock-corded tent pole together: unfold each section, let the cord pull both joints home, leave it straight
context: Anyone who has pitched a modern tent has put a shock-corded pole together: the sections are strung on an elastic cord that keeps them in order and pulls each joint home once the tubes line up. The same cord makes the folded pole awkward: every section is tied to its neighbour, its end is pulled against the next tube while it is swung round, and an insert that is not lined up will not go in, so a joint left part-way lets the pole kink when the tent is tensioned. This is the full-size named retail pole, three 38 cm sections making 114 cm, with its own cord; nothing is scaled down and no joint is tuned. The hands only ever hold the tubes, as a camper's do, and the pole stays on the table as one put together on the ground: one hand holds the part already in line while the other swings the next section round, lines its insert up and lets the cord draw it home.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (bases at x 0, y +-0.305), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. One Six Moon Designs 45 in Ultralight Tent Pole, aluminium, 3-section (maker: 114 cm assembled, 43 cm folded, 85 g, 3/8 in tube; USD 15): three dark grey anodised aluminium tubes, each 380 mm long, 9.5 mm across with an 8.1 mm bore, 28 g (bore and mass split: estimates). The right end section A and the middle section M each carry a bare aluminium insert 7.9 mm across (estimate) at the same end, showing 50 mm, its last 3.5 mm tapered; M's other end and the left end section B's near end are open. A black shock cord runs inside all three, knotted in the two outer ends (pull 3.0 N assembled, 4.0 N with both joints folded: estimates). Start: folded and laid flat on the bare table, the tubes side by side. M along y at x 0.150, its open end at y -0.190, its insert from y 0.190 to 0.240. B beside M at x 0.160, its open end at y 0.240 against M's insert, its free end at y -0.140. A outermost: its insert's tip at (0.159, -0.190) against M's open end, the tube running at 12 degrees off the y axis to its free end at (0.249, 0.230), just clear of B's free end. Tape marks on the table at the four ends of M and A. Nothing else on the table; x up to 0.60 is kept clear for the swings. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. Assembled, the pole lies along y near x 0.15 from y -0.57 to 0.57 (the table is 1.30 m wide, y -0.65 to 0.65).
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial from the top-camera video, a photograph, a steel rule and a 1.2 m straight edge; only the result counts. An insert has entered when its tip is inside the next tube's mouth; the gap g of a joint is the length of insert still showing between the two tube ends, by rule. Score 0 if neither insert has entered (doing nothing scores 0) or if any part of the pole leaves the table at any time. Otherwise the lowest of: (1) Joints home: 1.0 if both entered and both g <= 1 mm; 0.75 if both g <= 5 mm but not both <= 1 mm; 0.5 if both entered and a gap is over 5 mm; 0.25 if exactly one entered. (2) Straight: lay the straight edge from tip to tip and take d, the largest sideways distance to the pole's centre line: 1.0 if d <= 5 mm; 0.5 if 5 mm < d <= 20 mm; 0.25 if d > 20 mm or a joint has not entered. (3) Let go and still: 1.0 if both grippers' centre points are at least 3 cm from the pole and no point of it moves more than 3 mm during the last 1 s; 0.5 if they are 3 cm clear but it moves more; 0.25 if a gripper is within 3 cm (holding or touching it). The bands have exact limits and cover every case.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 seconds at 20 steps per second)
reset_notes: About 20 s. Pull each joint apart by its tubes against the cord, fold the end sections back beside the middle one and lay the pole on its tape marks: M on its line, B against M with its open end beside M's insert, A outermost with its insert's tip against M's open end and its free end on its mark. Check that the cord is inside the tubes and not frayed at the joints and that no tube or insert is bent; every 50 trials hang the folded pole's end section from a luggage scale and replace the pole if a joint opens under 2 N (cord gone slack). No consumables. Simulation reset restores the same folded layout with the cord at its folded pull.
fidelity: Three rigid 12-sided aluminium tubes at true size and mass; no tube flex. The shock cord is not a body: it is a tension line (8.5 N/m; 3.0 N assembled, 4.0 N folded: estimates) from one outer end through each insert tip and tube mouth to the other, recomputed 240 times a second. It pulls the joints together, has no contact, weight or friction, cannot be gripped and is drawn only where it shows at an open joint. Insert in bore: rigid, 0.2-0.5 mm clearance (estimate).
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (both joints home, pole straight within 1 mm, both hands clear and the pole still; full score from 28.9 s). Wrong way (left section let go about 95 degrees out of line): 0.25, one joint. Dream-1: 0.0 (pushed the folded sections about; no joint made).
